_notes: Taito do Brasil Oba-Oba (1980) on the later hardware: the 1979 firmware moved up to the 0x4000 window. It keeps
the 1979 structure - credits display at 0x408F, player count at 0x408D - but puts settings, high score and
stored credits where the 1981-85 boards do (0x4070, 0x4079, 0x407F). Compiled 2026-10 by evilwraith from the ROM
code and live obaoba captures on an AtGames ALP4K (Visual Pinball Standalone): a full one-player game read back
its final score of 16,312 (held in 0x40F4 afterwards) and two credits, with 0x408D at 1 and 0x408F at 2
throughout; later sessions added a four-player game, replays at both levels, extra balls and a beaten high
score. obaoba1 - ROM code references every declared address identically.
Display scores are three BCD bytes least-significant first (platform endian: little); 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF is a blank
display. The nine-byte BCD settings block is edited from the service menu and validated at reset (a non-BCD byte
restores all nine from ROM); its entries are named from the Shock (1979) and Cosmic (1981) operator sheets.
No checksum or mirror. The firmware deliberately resumes a game in progress at reset, so an image saved mid-game
holds that game: game_over clear and a ball in play.
0x40F4-0x40FF holds the last game's final display (four scores, same encoding as 0x4080) once the game is over, while the attract alternates the live display between it and the high score.

Audits are 16-bit little-endian binary counters from +50, which the statistics display walks two bytes at a time (Vortex 0x08BB). Seven are declared, two of them past +5F; +50, +58 and +5A read zero in every capture.

player_count._notes: 1979-style position; 1 throughout a live one-player game, 0 in attract. The reset path refuses to resume with 5 or more here.
player_count.label: Players

current_player._notes: One bit per player - 1, 2, 4, 8 for players one to four, 0 in attract - which the values list turns into the player number. The firmware finds the number by rotating the byte right until the carry sets and compares it with the player count (Oba-Oba 0x0CBE). Live in a four-player game: 1, 2, 4, 8.
current_player.label: Current Player

credits._notes: Stored value; the firmware keeps a display copy at 0x408F (1979-style), 2 in both during the live game.
credits.label: Credits

match._notes: Match digit shown after the game; cycles 0-9 during play (the randomiser). Reads 0xFF in attract before any game on this firmware.
match.label: Match

game_over._notes: Bit 0 of the firmware's flags byte: set in attract and by its reset path when it declines to resume, clear during a game.
game_over.label: Game Over

tilted._notes: Bit 1 of the flags byte. Pulsed briefly once mid-ball with scoring continuing (the tilt warning), then set and held from the real tilt on ball 5 until the game ended (live).
tilted.label: Tilted

score._notes: Most-significant byte first, unlike the display; the reset path reloads it from the ROM's minimum if it reads lower.

01._notes: Labels and ranges from the Shock (1979) and Cosmic (1981) operator sheets; byte positions and defaults match every image captured. Defaults are each set's own factory table, read from its ROM (the ten bytes the reset path copies in when a settings byte is not BCD).
01.label: Balls Per Game

02._notes: 'Fichas/Partida' (Cosmic: 'Credito/Partida'). A two-digit code, not a count: the sheets allow 11-14 and list 15 as a forbidden value that forces the default. What the digits mean is not stated on either sheet.
02.label: Coinage (code)

03._notes: 'Credito/Maximo'. The firmware clamps the stored credits to this value at boot.
03.label: Maximum Credits

04._notes: 'Incentivo'; the sheets allow 01 and 11-14. The 1980 firmware (drakor, meteort, fireact and the Oba-Oba sets) holds 04 here, outside that set, so its meaning there is not confirmed.
04.label: Incentive

05._notes: '1o Score' on the sheets, 15 to 99 on Shock's: one BCD byte in tens of thousands (scale), compared with the score's two most-significant digits by the same routine in every set. Set and played live at 150,000 and 180,000.
05.label: Replay Level 1

06._notes: '2o Score'. Skipped when equal to adjustment 5 (the Shock sheet says so, and the routine compares them).
06.label: Replay Level 2

07._notes: 'Bola Extra Score' on the sheets. The firmware compares the score with this level and, unless it equals adjustment 6, jumps once per player per game into a per-game hook (vector 0x1BCC), which awards an extra ball: in live games every player who passed the level (five times, at 150,000 and 200,000, one of them player four of a four-player game) was served the same ball again after the drain. The ball number does not change.
07.label: Extra Ball Score

09._notes: 'Credito/Record': credits awarded for beating the high score.
09.label: Credits For High Score

01._notes: Ticks only while a game is running (live on Drakor and Oba-Oba), about every 64 s like the powered-on timer. The statistics display divides it by games played for an average game time.
01.label: Play Time (ticks)

02._notes: Ticks about every 64 s whether or not a game is running (Vortex in attract: 44, 108, 173, 237, 301 s).
02.label: Powered-On Time (ticks)

03._notes: One tick per coin, on the same poll the credit rose. In a second capture three coins - two of them entered through chutes 2 and 3 - all ticked this counter and no other, so it is either a total or the table routes every coin key to one switch.
03.label: Coins

04._notes: Ticks once per player started, as each credit is consumed: a four-player start took credits 4 to 0 and ticked this four times (live on Oba-Oba). One tick at game start in the five single-player captures.
04.label: Games Played

05._notes: Ticks once per credit the game awards: at each replay level passed, for whichever player is up (live at 150,000/400,000 and at 180,000/300,000 as configured, including player four of a four-player game), and by the two credits given for beating the high score - a 605,893 game against 580,000 raised it by 4 (two replay levels, two high-score credits). Measured on Oba-Oba.
05.label: Credits Awarded

06._notes: Moved in step with Credits Awarded through nine replay-level awards, then by 2 where that rose by 4 in the game that beat the high score - so it excludes the high-score credits. Measured on Oba-Oba only.
06.label: Replays Awarded

07._notes: Zero until a game beat the high score (605,893 against 580,000), then 2 - the 'credits for high score' setting. One observation, from RAM before and after the game rather than a frame-by-frame capture. Measured on Oba-Oba only.
07.label: High Score Credits Awarded
